item.research_question: How does substrate surface roughness affect the geometry and hardness of laser-cladded Fe-based metallic glass single tracks, and can a fuzzy logic control system optimize these properties?
item.material_system: Fe-based amorphous powder (MG) cladded on F2229 stainless steel substrate
item.processing_route: Laser cladding using a 4.4 kW high-power diode laser (wavelength 978–1025 ± 10 nm) with fixed parameters: 2000 W laser power, 45 mm/s scanning speed, and 4 × 4 mm² spot size; substrate surfaces prepared via SiC sandpaper polishing (SP150, SP240) or Al2O3 sandblasting (SB40, SB100) with a 300 μm preplaced powder layer under Argon flow
item.test_conditions: Substrate surface roughness varied by preparation method (SP vs. SB) and grit size (150, 240, 40, 100); geometry (height L1, width L2) and hardness measured for single tracks
key_findings: Substrate surface roughness significantly affected the geometry and hardness of the laser-cladded Fe-based MG single track.
Polished substrates exhibited higher hardness values than sandblasted samples.
The amorphous content percentage increased with increasing substrate surface roughness.
Surface roughness of the substrate was found to decrease due to superior cohesion force over adhesion force, leading to an increment in the width and height of the cladded track.
The fuzzy logic control system yielded the best results for SP240 (sandpaper grit size 240), agreeing with experimental data.
The fuzzy logic control system results were located between the experimental data values, demonstrating agreement.
The polished substrate yielded optimum results in terms of geometry and hardness.
item.mechanism: The authors argue that due to superior cohesion force over adhesion force between the molten coating material and the substrate, the surface roughness of the substrate decreases, which leads to an increment in the width and height of the cladded track. Conversely, the amorphous content percentage increases with increasing substrate surface roughness, which affects the hardness, with polished substrates showing higher hardness values.
item.limitations: The authors state that FLC has two significant shortcomings: it is unable to handle ambiguous data and comprehend human thought.
item.future_work: The work may be further extended to examine the strength and degree of thermal insulation in the cladded parts for structural applications.
quotes: The experiment showed that substrate surface roughness affected the geometry and hardness of laser-cladded Fe-based MG.
Hardness measurements showed that the polished substrate exhibited higher hardness values than the sandblasted samples.
The fuzzy logic control system yielded the best results for SP 240 (sandpaper grit size 240), thus agreeing with experimental data.
